title: Sometimes auto-plan doesn't pick up ideating phases
description: It seems like sometimes the auto-plan just ... stops looking at the dieating phase.  It was after a long period of rate-limiting, so maybe it was backing off more and more or something?  Or got stuck?  I'm not sure.  But it was sitting idle, even though it was no longer rate-limited and there were six things in the ideating section
plan:
## Root Cause Analysis

The auto-plan queue tracking mechanism uses a set that functions as a permanent blacklist rather than an in-flight tracker. Three distinct failure modes cause items to become permanently stuck:

1. **Exception-path failure (ideating):** When ideation encounters any error (rate limits, JSON parse errors, file I/O failures), the item remains in the queue forever because cleanup only runs on the success path. The rate-limit handler sets a cooldown timer but never removes the item from the queue, so after the cooldown expires the item is still blacklisted.

2. **Missing cleanup (planning/review):** The planning async worker has no cleanup call whatsoever — not on success, not on failure, not in its finally block. Every plan-inbox and reviewing-plan item that gets processed is permanently stuck in the queue after its first attempt, even when it completes successfully. This is a fundamental design gap where the cleanup path was simply never implemented for this workflow.

3. **Worker cancellation (timing-dependent):** Both the ideation and planning async workers share the same exclusive worker group. The framework silently cancels a running worker when a new one starts in the same group. If auto-plan triggers a second worker before the first completes, the cancelled worker never reaches its cleanup call, creating another permanent stuck entry. This makes the bug intermittent and timing-dependent.

Over time, all items that encounter any of these three paths accumulate in the blacklist, progressively disabling auto-plan until it appears to have stopped working entirely.

## Impact Assessment

- **Severity: High.** This effectively disables a core automation feature over time. The more items processed, the worse it gets.
- **User-visible behavior:** Auto-plan appears to silently stop processing items despite them being in eligible stages. The TUI shows no errors — it simply skips everything.
- **Scope of impact:** Affects all three auto-plan eligible stages (ideating, plan-inbox, reviewing-plan). The planning/review path is 100% broken (every item gets stuck), while ideating is broken on any error.
- **Related risk:** The auto-implement queue uses a similar pattern and should be audited for the same class of bug.

## Fix Strategy

1. **Ensure cleanup runs on all exit paths:** Move queue removal into a finally block (or equivalent guaranteed-execution pattern) for all async workers that participate in auto-plan. This covers success, exceptions, rate limits, and early returns.

2. **Add resilience against transient failures:** Rather than permanently blacklisting items after a single attempt, consider either (a) a retry counter that allows N attempts before giving up, or (b) a time-based expiry so items become eligible again after a cooldown period. This prevents transient errors (rate limits, network blips) from permanently disabling processing for an item.

3. **Address the worker cancellation race:** Either handle the cancellation signal explicitly to ensure cleanup runs, or re-evaluate whether the exclusive worker group constraint is appropriate. Serializing auto-plan triggers (e.g., via a queue or flag check) could prevent the race entirely.

## Risks

- **Retry storms:** If cleanup is too aggressive (always removing from queue immediately), a persistently failing item could be retried every auto-plan cycle, creating a hot loop. The retry counter or cooldown approach mitigates this.
- **Race conditions:** Changing the exclusive worker group or adding cancellation handling needs careful testing to avoid introducing new timing bugs.
- **State consistency:** The queue cleanup must be thread-safe since async workers run in background threads but the queue is accessed from the main thread.

## Scope

- **In scope:** Fixing queue cleanup for all three async worker paths (ideating, planning, pipeline). Adding retry/expiry logic to prevent permanent blacklisting. Auditing the auto-implement queue for the same pattern.
- **Out of scope:** Changing the auto-plan scheduling algorithm, modifying the rate-limit backoff strategy, or restructuring the worker threading model beyond what's needed for the fix.

## Implementation Spec: Fix auto-plan queue permanent blacklisting

All changes are in `pipeline/tui.py` unless noted otherwise.

### Task 1: Move queue cleanup into finally blocks for all async workers

**Status: Partially applied in working tree. Verify and finalize.**

The committed code has queue cleanup (`discard`) only on success paths (via `_on_plan_done`/`_on_implement_done` callbacks). Items that fail, get rate-limited, or have their worker cancelled are permanently stuck in the queue.

**Changes needed in `_run_ideating_async` (~line 3785):**
- Add `self._auto_plan_queued.discard(feature.slug)` to the `finally` block
- Add `self._auto_plan_queued.discard(feature.slug)` to the lock-failure early return path (before `return`)
- Remove the `self.app.call_from_thread(self._on_plan_done, feature.slug)` from the success path inside `try` (cleanup now happens in `finally`)
- Add `self.app.call_from_thread(self._refresh_board, self.active_board)` to the `finally` block to ensure UI refresh happens on all exit paths

**Changes needed in `_run_plan_async` (~line 3713):**
- Add `self._auto_plan_queued.discard(feature.slug)` to the `finally` block
- Add `self._auto_plan_queued.discard(feature.slug)` to the lock-failure early return path (before `return`)

**Changes needed in `_run_implement_async` (~line 3856):**
- Add `self._auto_implement_queued.discard(feature.slug)` to the `finally` block
- Add `self._auto_implement_queued.discard(feature.slug)` to the lock-failure early return path (before `return`)
- Replace the `self.app.call_from_thread(self._on_implement_done, feature.slug)` at the end of `finally` with `self.app.call_from_thread(self._refresh_board, self.active_board)` (cleanup now in finally)

**Changes needed in `_run_pipeline_async` (~line 3660):**
- Add queue cleanup to the `finally` block, dispatching to the correct queue based on feature stage:
  ```python
  if feature.current_stage in ("plan-inbox", "reviewing-plan", "requested-input", "approved", "spec-writing"):
      self._auto_plan_queued.discard(feature.slug)
  else:
      self._auto_implement_queued.discard(feature.slug)
  ```

**Changes needed in `_on_plan_done` and `_on_implement_done`:**
- Remove `self._plan_running = False` and `self._auto_plan_queued.discard(slug)` from `_on_plan_done` (now handled in finally blocks)
- Remove `self._implement_running = False` and `self._auto_implement_queued.discard(slug)` from `_on_implement_done` (now handled in finally blocks)
- These callbacks become purely UI refresh/notification methods

### Task 2: Add retry cooldown to prevent retry storms

With Task 1, failed items are removed from the queue and become eligible again immediately on the next `_auto_plan_check` cycle. A persistently failing item would be retried every `AUTO_RUN_INTERVAL` seconds, creating a hot loop.

**Add a failure cooldown dict alongside the queue set:**

In `__init__` (around line 1947-1948), add:
```python
self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown: dict[str, float] = {}   # slug -> timestamp when eligible again
self._auto_implement_fail_cooldown: dict[str, float] = {}  # slug -> timestamp when eligible again
```

Define a cooldown constant (near `AUTO_RUN_INTERVAL`):
```python
AUTO_RETRY_COOLDOWN = 120  # seconds before retrying a failed item
AUTO_MAX_RETRIES = 5  # max consecutive failures before permanent skip until restart
```

Also add a failure counter:
```python
self._auto_plan_fail_count: dict[str, int] = {}   # slug -> consecutive failure count
self._auto_implement_fail_count: dict[str, int] = {}  # slug -> consecutive failure count
```

**Modify `_auto_plan_check` (~line 3462):**
After the existing `if f.slug in self._auto_plan_queued: continue` check, add:
```python
# Skip items in cooldown after failure
now_ts = time.time()
if f.slug in self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown:
    if now_ts < self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown[f.slug]:
        logger.info(f"[auto-plan] Skipping {f.slug} - in failure cooldown")
        continue
    else:
        # Cooldown expired, remove from cooldown dict
        del self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown[f.slug]
# Skip items that have exceeded max retries
if self._auto_plan_fail_count.get(f.slug, 0) >= self.AUTO_MAX_RETRIES:
    logger.info(f"[auto-plan] Skipping {f.slug} - exceeded max retries ({self.AUTO_MAX_RETRIES})")
    continue
```

**Modify `_auto_implement_check` (~line 3514):**
Same pattern as above but using `_auto_implement_fail_cooldown` and `_auto_implement_fail_count`.

**Record failures in async workers:**

In `_run_ideating_async`, in the `except RateLimitError` and `except Exception` blocks, set cooldown:
```python
self._auto_plan_fail_count[feature.slug] = self._auto_plan_fail_count.get(feature.slug, 0) + 1
self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown[feature.slug] = time.time() + self.AUTO_RETRY_COOLDOWN
```

Same pattern in `_run_plan_async` exception handlers.

Same pattern in `_run_implement_async` exception handlers using `_auto_implement_fail_*`.

**Clear failure count on success:**

At the end of the `try` block (success path) in each async worker, clear the failure tracking:
```python
self._auto_plan_fail_count.pop(feature.slug, None)
self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown.pop(feature.slug, None)
```

This ensures items that succeed after previous failures get a clean slate.

### Task 3: Add debug logging for queue state

In `_auto_plan_check`, after the existing logging of stage counts, add:
```python
if self._auto_plan_queued:
    logger.info(f"[auto-plan] Currently queued: {self._auto_plan_queued}")
if self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown:
    logger.info(f"[auto-plan] In cooldown: {list(self._auto_plan_fail_cooldown.keys())}")
```

Same for `_auto_implement_check` with the implement variants.

This makes it easy to diagnose stuck-item issues from logs.

### Task 4: Audit auto-implement queue for same bug pattern

The auto-implement queue (`_auto_implement_queued`) has the same class of bug in the committed code:
- `_run_implement_async` calls `_on_implement_done` (which does `discard`) only at the end of the `finally` block, but only on the non-restart path. Rate-limit and exception paths don't reach it.
- Lock-failure early return doesn't clean up the queue.

The fix is identical to Task 1: move `discard` into the `finally` block and the lock-failure early return. This is covered by the `_run_implement_async` changes in Task 1.

### Task 5: Handle worker cancellation explicitly (optional/low priority)

Both `_run_ideating_async` and `_run_plan_async` use `@work(exclusive=True, group="plan")`. When Textual cancels a worker in an exclusive group, it sets `worker.is_cancelled = True` but does NOT interrupt the thread. The thread runs to completion, and the `finally` block executes. With `discard` in `finally` (Task 1), cancelled workers DO clean up properly.

However, a cancelled worker continues running its full operation uselessly. To avoid wasted API calls, consider checking `self.workers` cancellation state in long-running operations. This is low priority since the cleanup fix in Task 1 prevents the permanent-stuck-item bug.

If implemented, add periodic cancellation checks in `run_ideating`, `run_planning`, and `run_plan_review` in `pipeline/phases.py`:
```python
# At start of each major operation step
if hasattr(status, '_worker') and status._worker.is_cancelled:
    raise WorkerCancelled()
```

This is optional and can be deferred.

### Dependency order

1. Task 1 (queue cleanup in finally blocks) - core fix, no dependencies
2. Task 2 (retry cooldown) - depends on Task 1 being complete
3. Task 3 (debug logging) - can be done alongside Task 1 or 2
4. Task 4 (audit auto-implement) - covered by Task 1 changes to `_run_implement_async`
5. Task 5 (worker cancellation) - optional, independent

### Files to modify

- `pipeline/tui.py` - All changes (Tasks 1-4)
- `pipeline/phases.py` - Only if Task 5 is implemented (optional)

### Testing strategy

- Verify that after a rate-limit error on an ideating item, the item becomes eligible for auto-plan again after cooldown
- Verify that after a general exception on planning, the item becomes eligible again after cooldown
- Verify that successfully completed items are immediately removed from queue and not retried
- Verify that items exceeding MAX_RETRIES are skipped until TUI restart
- Verify that lock-failure early returns properly clean up the queue
- Check logs to confirm debug logging shows queue state correctly
test_spec:
# Test Specification: Fix auto-plan queue permanent blacklisting

## 1. Behaviors That MUST Be Verified

### 1.1 Queue cleanup on ideating success path
- **Behavior:** When `_run_ideating_async` completes successfully, the item's slug is removed from `_auto_plan_queued`.
- **Success criteria:** After successful ideation, `_auto_plan_queued` no longer contains the item's slug. The item becomes eligible for auto-plan processing again on the next cycle if it's still in an eligible stage.
- **Expected output:** The slug is discarded from the set; subsequent `_auto_plan_check` calls do not skip the item due to queue membership.

### 1.2 Queue cleanup on ideating failure path
- **Behavior:** When `_run_ideating_async` encounters any exception (JSON parse error, file I/O error, general exception), the item's slug is still removed from `_auto_plan_queued` via the finally block.
- **Success criteria:** After an exception during ideation, `_auto_plan_queued` does not permanently contain the failed item's slug. The item enters a failure cooldown instead of being permanently blacklisted.
- **Expected output:** Slug is discarded from the queue set; a cooldown entry is created in `_auto_plan_fail_cooldown`.

### 1.3 Queue cleanup on ideating rate-limit path
- **Behavior:** When `_run_ideating_async` encounters a rate-limit error, the item's slug is removed from `_auto_plan_queued` via the finally block, and a cooldown is set.
- **Success criteria:** After a rate-limit error, the item is not permanently stuck. It enters cooldown and becomes eligible again after the cooldown period expires.
- **Expected output:** Slug discarded from queue; cooldown entry created; item retried after cooldown expires.

### 1.4 Queue cleanup on plan-async success path
- **Behavior:** When `_run_plan_async` completes successfully (for plan-inbox or reviewing-plan items), the item's slug is removed from `_auto_plan_queued` in the finally block.
- **Success criteria:** Successfully planned items are removed from the queue and do not accumulate as permanent entries.
- **Expected output:** Slug discarded; item not skipped on future auto-plan cycles.

### 1.5 Queue cleanup on plan-async failure path
- **Behavior:** When `_run_plan_async` encounters an exception, the finally block still removes the item from `_auto_plan_queued`.
- **Success criteria:** Failed planning items enter cooldown rather than being permanently blacklisted.
- **Expected output:** Slug discarded from queue; failure cooldown entry created.

### 1.6 Queue cleanup on lock acquisition failure
- **Behavior:** When any async worker (`_run_ideating_async`, `_run_plan_async`, `_run_implement_async`) fails to acquire its lock, the item's slug is discarded from the appropriate queue before returning.
- **Success criteria:** Lock contention does not cause permanent queue accumulation. The item becomes eligible again on the next auto-plan cycle.
- **Expected output:** Slug discarded immediately; no cooldown needed since no work was attempted.

### 1.7 Queue cleanup on pipeline-async completion
- **Behavior:** `_run_pipeline_async` dispatches cleanup to the correct queue based on the feature's current stage (plan queue for plan-inbox/reviewing-plan/approved/spec-writing stages, implement queue for others).
- **Success criteria:** Items processed through the pipeline path are cleaned up from the correct queue regardless of success or failure.
- **Expected output:** Correct queue (`_auto_plan_queued` or `_auto_implement_queued`) has the slug discarded.

### 1.8 Implement queue cleanup (audit parity)
- **Behavior:** `_run_implement_async` has the same finally-block cleanup pattern as the plan workers. The item's slug is removed from `_auto_implement_queued` on all exit paths (success, failure, rate-limit, lock failure).
- **Success criteria:** The auto-implement queue does not exhibit the same permanent blacklisting bug that affected auto-plan.
- **Expected output:** Slug discarded from `_auto_implement_queued` on all exit paths.

### 1.9 Retry cooldown prevents hot loops
- **Behavior:** When an item fails, it enters a cooldown period (AUTO_RETRY_COOLDOWN seconds). During cooldown, `_auto_plan_check` skips the item. After cooldown expires, the item becomes eligible again.
- **Success criteria:** A failing item is not retried on every auto-plan cycle. It is skipped during cooldown and retried only after the cooldown period.
- **Expected output:** Item skipped with log message during cooldown; item processed again after cooldown expires.

### 1.10 Max retry limit prevents infinite retries
- **Behavior:** After AUTO_MAX_RETRIES consecutive failures, the item is permanently skipped until the TUI is restarted (failure count resets on restart since it's in-memory).
- **Success criteria:** An item that fails repeatedly is eventually stopped from retrying. It does not create an infinite retry loop.
- **Expected output:** After MAX_RETRIES failures, item is skipped with a log message indicating max retries exceeded.

### 1.11 Success clears failure tracking
- **Behavior:** When an item that previously failed eventually succeeds, its failure count and cooldown entries are cleared.
- **Success criteria:** A transient failure followed by success does not leave stale failure tracking data. The item gets a clean slate.
- **Expected output:** `_auto_plan_fail_count` and `_auto_plan_fail_cooldown` no longer contain the item's slug after success.

### 1.12 Debug logging shows queue state
- **Behavior:** `_auto_plan_check` and `_auto_implement_check` log the current queue contents and cooldown state when non-empty.
- **Success criteria:** When items are in the queue or in cooldown, log messages show which items are queued and which are in cooldown.
- **Expected output:** Log entries like `[auto-plan] Currently queued: {'slug1', 'slug2'}` and `[auto-plan] In cooldown: ['slug3']`.

## 2. Edge Cases

### 2.1 Empty queue state
- When no items are queued or in cooldown, `_auto_plan_check` should proceed normally without logging queue/cooldown state (no noise in logs for normal operation).

### 2.2 Item moves to a non-eligible stage between queue add and worker start
- If an item is added to `_auto_plan_queued` but moves to a different stage (e.g., manually moved by user) before the worker starts, the finally block should still clean up the queue entry. The item should not remain stuck.

### 2.3 Concurrent failures across multiple items
- Multiple items failing simultaneously should each get their own independent cooldown timer and failure count. One item's failure should not affect another item's eligibility.

### 2.4 Cooldown expiry exactly at check time
- When the cooldown timer expires at the exact moment `_auto_plan_check` runs, the item should be processed (the expired cooldown entry should be removed and the item should be eligible).

### 2.5 Failure count at exactly MAX_RETRIES
- An item with exactly MAX_RETRIES failures should be skipped. An item with MAX_RETRIES - 1 failures should still be retried.

### 2.6 TUI restart clears all in-memory state
- Since `_auto_plan_queued`, `_auto_plan_fail_cooldown`, and `_auto_plan_fail_count` are all in-memory, restarting the TUI should reset all tracking, giving all items a fresh start.

### 2.7 Worker cancellation via exclusive group
- When two workers in the same exclusive group (e.g., ideating then planning) are triggered in quick succession, the first worker is cancelled by Textual. The cancelled worker's finally block should still execute and clean up the queue entry.

### 2.8 Rate-limit followed by successful retry
- An item that gets rate-limited should enter cooldown, then after cooldown expires, should be retried. If the retry succeeds, the failure count should be cleared.

### 2.9 Lock held by external process
- When the pipeline lock is held by another process (e.g., CLI pipeline run), the async worker should fail to acquire the lock, discard from queue, and allow the item to be retried on the next cycle.

### 2.10 Queue cleanup thread safety
- `_auto_plan_queued.discard()` is called from background threads (async workers) while `_auto_plan_queued` is read from the main thread (`_auto_plan_check`). Set operations in Python are GIL-protected, but verify no race conditions exist with the cooldown/failure dicts.

## 3. What Constitutes Failure

### 3.1 Permanent queue accumulation
- **FAILURE:** If any item remains in `_auto_plan_queued` or `_auto_implement_queued` indefinitely after its worker has finished (regardless of success or failure), the fix has not addressed the core bug.

### 3.2 Hot retry loop
- **FAILURE:** If a consistently failing item is retried on every `_auto_plan_check` cycle without any cooldown delay, the retry protection is broken.

### 3.3 Items never retried after transient failure
- **FAILURE:** If an item that experienced a single transient error (rate limit, network blip) is never retried, the fix has overcorrected. Items should become eligible again after cooldown.

### 3.4 Wrong queue cleanup
- **FAILURE:** If `_run_pipeline_async` discards from the wrong queue (e.g., discards from plan queue for an implementing item, or vice versa), items will appear stuck in one queue while being cleaned from another.

### 3.5 Missing finally block
- **FAILURE:** If any async worker path (ideating, plan, implement, pipeline) lacks a finally block with queue cleanup, there exist exit paths that can permanently blacklist items.

### 3.6 Failure tracking not cleared on success
- **FAILURE:** If an item succeeds after previous failures but its failure count is not reset, it will hit MAX_RETRIES prematurely on future failures.

### 3.7 Silent skip without logging
- **FAILURE:** If items are being skipped due to queue membership, cooldown, or max retries, but no log message is emitted, debugging will be as difficult as before the fix.

## 4. Out of Scope

- **TUI rendering and visual assertions:** Do not test that the UI displays correct queue state visually. Only verify the underlying data structures.
- **Auto-plan scheduling algorithm:** Do not test the order in which items are picked for processing or the interval timing beyond cooldown behavior.
- **Rate-limit backoff strategy:** Do not test the specific backoff timing for rate limits. Only verify that rate-limited items are cleaned up from the queue.
- **Worker threading model:** Do not test Textual's exclusive worker group implementation. Only verify that the application-level cleanup handles cancellation correctly.
- **Performance benchmarks:** Do not test how fast queue operations are or how many items can be processed per cycle.
- **Pipeline execution correctness:** Do not test that ideation, planning, or implementation produce correct outputs. Only test queue lifecycle management.
- **External process lock contention:** Do not test the lock file mechanism itself. Only verify that lock acquisition failure triggers proper queue cleanup.
- **UI refresh after cleanup:** Do not test that the board view refreshes correctly after queue cleanup. Only verify the queue state is correct.

Ideation:
The core bug is that `_auto_plan_queued` in tui.py acts as a permanent blacklist rather than an in-flight tracker. Items are added when auto-plan picks them up, but are only removed on successful completion of `_run_ideating_async` (via `_on_plan_done`). This means any item that fails — due to JSON parse errors, rate limits, file I/O failures, or exceptions — gets permanently stuck in the queue and can never be retried. Over time, all items that have ever encountered any error accumulate in `_auto_plan_queued`, effectively disabling auto-plan for those items forever.

Beyond the exception-path bug, there is a critical happy-path failure: `_run_plan_async` (used for plan-inbox and reviewing-plan items) never calls `_on_plan_done` in any code path — not on success, not on failure, not in a finally block. This means every plan-inbox and reviewing-plan item is permanently stuck in `_auto_plan_queued` after its first processing attempt, even when it completes successfully. Only `_run_ideating_async` calls `_on_plan_done`, and only on success. This represents a fundamental design gap where the cleanup path was simply never implemented for plan-inbox/reviewing-plan workflows.

A third failure mode involves the shared `@work(exclusive=True, group="plan")` decorator on both `_run_ideating_async` and `_run_plan_async`. Textual will silently cancel a running worker if a new one starts in the same exclusive group. If auto-plan triggers a second worker before the first completes, the cancelled worker never reaches its `_on_plan_done` call, causing another permanent stuck entry. This makes the bug timing-dependent and intermittent, explaining why it doesn't always manifest.

The fix requires ensuring `_on_plan_done` (or equivalent cleanup) is called in a `finally` block for all async workers, covering success, failure, and cancellation paths. Additionally, consideration should be given to whether `_auto_plan_queued` should use a time-based expiry or a retry counter rather than permanent exclusion, so transient errors (rate limits, network failures) don't permanently disable auto-plan for affected items. The exclusive worker group constraint should also be re-evaluated — either by serializing auto-plan triggers or by handling cancellation explicitly.
